dialogue.text: Morning, Marcus. Certainly, we can keep this practical. First, may I have your identification details for our verification checks? Please make sure you're somewhere private.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you. So your aim is to reduce your technology exposure and free up cash for the business. For the transaction currency, we can use Japanese yen.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: By the way, telephone is still the easiest way to reach me. During the day I'm usually between client meetings, and a long email chain tends to get buried.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: All right, I'll note that preference as well. You can check the mailbox when you're back at your desk; there's no need to involve your office staff in collecting correspondence.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That arrangement suits me. Use the currency you mentioned earlier for this transaction. The amount for this transaction is 7,500,000. The quantity to transact is 1,000 units.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll keep the account correspondence separate from your general business mail. For telephone contact, would you prefer that I leave only a brief callback message if you're unavailable?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, just your name and a request to call back, please. No account details in voicemail. I want to sell that holding. Place it as a market order, please.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Noted. We'll use the contact details already on file and keep any message brief. I'll come back to you when there's an update from the review.
